newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Amaury plans TV sports news channel-paper.
newsitem.headline: France's Amaury plans TV sports news channel-paper.

text.p: Amaury, the French press group which owns sports daily L'Equipe and popular daily Le Parisien, is planning to launch a television sports news channel, financial daily Les Echos said on Monday.
It quoted Jerome Bureau, director of L'Equipe and L'Equipe magazine, as saying the idea was inspired by the launch of the CNNSI channel by Time Warner's Cable News Network (CNN) last February.
An Amaury spokesman confirmed the report.
Amaury's project "is not a channel re-broadcasting sporting events like Eurosport, but a project based on the model of L'Equipe dealing with all sports," Les Echos quoted Bureau as saying.

Bureau said the sports news channel was being developed jointly by L'Equipe and Amaury Sports Organisation, which distributes sports television pictures including of the Tour de France, one of the sporting events which it organises.

The project was presented to the three French digital satellite television services, TF1's Television par Satellite (TPS), Canal Plus's CanalSatellite and AB Productions' AB Sat, in June, and its timing and budget depends on their response, the paper said.
Bureau said the channel's initial budget would be some 80 million francs, but this could be revised in the light of responses from the three digital operators.
Amaury does not plan to offer the channel exclusively to any one operator, the paper said.
Amaury's Le Parisien was named as a partner to Canal Plus in creating a television news channel to rival TF1's LCI in a report in financial daily La Tribune on August 6. Canal Plus declined comment.
